claims.value: Hormayr gives fewer than 20,000 Austrians including 2,300 cavalry, against thirteen enemy cavalry regiments and 40,000 infantry at the Piave.
claims.rationale: National narrative comparison, not matched own-side returns; unlike Bodart’s 25,000 Austrian available total. English rendering (ours): "Fewer than 20,000 Austrians, including only 2,300 cavalry, resisted thirteen enemy cavalry regiments and 40,000 infantry."

open_questions: Reconcile fewer-than-20,000 Austrian narrative strength with Bodart’s 25,000 and French available versus excluded contingents; establish exact crossing/arrival timing and local cavalry orders.
Deferred: original dated local returns and command reports; source-specific alternatives are not reconciled by averaging.
Dependence: Bodart is a later compilation; national/participant accounts are interested and mediated. Volumes, translations and embedded reports count within their assigned author/source family.

A.strength_population_and_time: Bodart is an available-for-engagement compilation unless a subset is expressly marked. Bodart: side A (French) 45,000; side B (Austrian) 25,000. Hormayr gives fewer than 20,000 Austrians including 2,300 cavalry, against thirteen enemy cavalry regiments and 40,000 infantry at the Piave. Pelet excludes part of Broussier’s division, three Durutte regiments and Fontanelli’s division from participation.
A.command_scope: Printed labels and local/superior authority observations remain distinct. Bodart lists side A under Eugène Beauharnais; side B under Archduke Johann. Pelet assigns Eugène the order to Sahuc/Pully to watch the enemy and the decision to defer pursuit until the rest crossed.
A.army_continuity: Unknown: no cross-engagement army identity established. Repeated commander/formation labels do not establish continuity.
